request.prompt:
VIEW 1 — THE WHOLE MAP FROM ABOVE THE COACH ROAD, LOOKING SOUTH.

ONE single full-frame view. Not a grid, not panels, not insets. No text, no labels, no interface.

The eye hangs about thirty blocks above the coach road at the north edge of the town and looks south and down across the whole map, under a bright full moon high in the southern sky.

Foreground and lower third: the town of Wrackham on cliff terraces falling toward the bay, about 160 blocks wide: a cobbled coach road along the top of the cliff with a small coach stop and a lantern post; below it a narrow high street of tall grey stone houses with steep slate roofs winding down; a small stone chapel with a squat bell tower partway down; at the bottom, a stone harbour with a seawall, a fish market roof, warehouses, net lofts and a long low rope shed. The harbour basin is empty of water: boats lie tilted on wet black mud. A stone breakwater runs out from the harbour's east side into the bay, ending in a tall white-and-grey stone lighthouse tower, its lamp unlit.

Middle third: where the bay should be, a vast flat plain of wet black mud stretches away south, about 320 blocks long, glistening in the moonlight, with shallow black sea water showing in channels and puddles. A faint line of wooden marker stakes runs straight out across the mud from the harbour toward the far end. Old wrecked hulls lie on their sides in the mud partway out, and a grounded salvage launch with a mast stands beside the stake line.

Far third: at the end of the mud a channel of open black sea water about sixty blocks wide crosses the whole frame, with a small stone ferry house with a slate roof on each shore. Beyond the channel, on its own low bank of mud, lies the creature: a hill-sized whale-like leviathan built of dark grey-green and black blocks, about 140 blocks long and 45 blocks high, lying on its belly with its head toward the town, its back a long ridged spine, its outline catching the moonlight. A thin sea mist lies over the far water.

Open ocean, flat and dark, fills the horizon all round. Stars in the sky.
request.style_note: The Stranding: every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand — a Minecraft Java Edition build shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft night shader. Every surface is made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (cobblestone, stone bricks, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, deepslate, mud and packed mud, black and grey concrete, prismarine, lanterns, glass panes), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round or organic forms are stepped block shapes. The place is a grey slate-roofed fishing town on cliff terraces above a bay, a plain of wet black mud risen from the bay, and a vast stranded sea creature built of dark blocks lying at the far edge of the mud. Night under a clear sky and a bright full moon: cold blue-silver moonlight on wet mud and slate roofs, deep blue-black shadows, small warm yellow pools of lantern light at doors and windows, sea water near-black with silver moon glints. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, no text, no labels, no border, no interface.
